claim: Cognitive Simulation (anima/simulation.py, Phase 22) lets you test a change on a DIGITAL TWIN before prod — ask what WOULD / MIGHT / SHOULD happen and actually run it, never touching the real mind. Four engines each return a measured, inspectable result + the twin it ran on: DECISION ('what SHOULD happen?' — grounded in how Lamar actually decides via Personal Intelligence + the World Model, an option that matches nothing in his captured model earns NO recommendation, never invented), LEARNING ('what WOULD happen if we learned X for T?' — synthetic accelerate, deterministic + $0, Off mode provably inert), ARCHITECTURE ('what WOULD happen if we changed retrieval?' — FMLGS-vs-keyword measured on the twin's own vault), and ALTERNATIVE FUTURES ('what MIGHT happen?' — a min/median/max range across independent forked futures). Every engine runs INSIDE twin.freeze_guard, which fingerprints the real Vera identity AND the whole real .anima before/after and ASSERTS both byte-identical (raising FreezeViolation otherwise).
owner: anima/simulation.py (simulate_decision / simulate_learning + compare_learning_plans / simulate_architecture / alternative_futures / what_happened, the simulate() router, worked_examples, and the hermetic _selftest; composes twin.py's PUBLIC API only — create_twin / accelerate / branch_futures / run_experiment / mri / freeze_guard — and runs every read/write inside twin._RedirectStores so engines touch the TWIN'S namespace), anima/twin.py (the freeze-safe twin substrate: create_twin / accelerate / branch_futures / freeze_guard / FreezeViolation). INTERNAL cognitive engine: NOT exposed via a server endpoint / route / web UI (server.py imports neither simulation nor twin; index.html has no simulate control).
